question: Which schema and renderer contracts should HTML ingress and static output share, and which interactive dependencies can be removed?
trigger: User supplied completed static-preview proportional-cost results and asked whether the next Best API Review should repeat this work or move to another item.
requirements: Reconcile the prior projected-read and image-title findings with subsequent implementation and current public-boundary behavior.
Retain completed source-bound parser/publication/static-renderer adoption without treating stale older receipts as a wholesale reset.
Rendering and decoration locations must identify the correct document root; identical local paths in distinct roots must not alias.
Use the existing root/view/location owner before adding public state or a new registry protocol; keep root-relative paths valid within a clearly bound root.
Distinguish measured runtime costs, correctness gaps and historical ledger status when ranking the next job.
Assessment and research history only; no product repair, implementation plan, staging or publication.
evidenceReuse: Read the completed proportional-cost plan and its bound execution outcome, matching current HTML review, pp3 and pp4 receipts, source and public callback contracts. Re-ran the original image-title scenario and a current public EditorStatic/renderStaticHtml TOC scenario; both now pass. The earlier projection probe itself imports a deleted private helper and is historical rather than current executable proof. Reused the completed browser measurements with their declared source scope and guard adjustment. This is a bounded next-work decision, not a new full conversion or Plite-view audit.
summary: Pursue content-root location context as the next architectural item; stop repeating the broad conversion/Markdown/streaming review. Coherent document reads and image-title preservation now pass direct public checks, and the proportional static-renderer program has matching execution evidence. DecorationSource.read still receives editor plus a root-relative NodeEntry with no root; static content-root traversal passes that entry against the same document editor. Static table cells resolve by node and index each document, while live list ordinal falls back to 1 when the node has no main-root path. Compare existing root-bound reader contexts with explicit root-qualified locations at the Plite owner, then remove redundant caller location recovery and detached traversal where justified. Keep converted-segment reuse, immutable document views, static reuse, registry customization and the measured decoration fixes. Per-block caching/chunking remains deferred by the existing cadence/product trigger. group-last utilities warrant direct UI performance repair, not another parser/API redesign. Remaining HTML list/subtree-accounting gaps are concrete follow-ups, not grounds for restarting every format.

reconciliation.question: Which schema and renderer contracts should HTML ingress and static output share, and which interactive dependencies can be removed?
reconciliation.reason: Retain the owner fixes, immutable document input and browser-based deferral of caching/chunking. The newer request adds no requirement that justifies another parser or full static-runtime replacement.

reconciliation.question: Which schema and renderer contracts should HTML ingress and static output share, and which interactive dependencies can be removed?
reconciliation.reason: Retain completed adoption and the final-tree source-bound receipts within the plan scope. Use its explicit root/location risks for the next architectural question. Preserve the pp4 attribution guard adjustment and remaining HTML fidelity limits rather than treating completion as universal correctness.

alternatives: Repeat the whole import/export/HTML/Markdown/streaming audit: Stop. The prior decisive bugs now pass, the settled parser/format contracts have no new contradictory requirement, and remaining failures have named narrower owners.

Keep root-relative NodeEntry without binding a root and patch list/table/decorations separately: Stop. Repeated location recovery retains ambiguity and indexing work across actual content-root consumers.

Change the existing Plite root/read context or pass an explicit root-qualified location through render/decorate callbacks: Pursue. Compare these two current-owner designs before choosing a signature; preserve local tuple iteration within a clearly bound root.
Add a new view manager, location registry or mirrored decoration store: Stop absent an independent job. Existing runtime roots and views own the identity.

Implement static per-block caching/chunking now: Defer under the accepted trigger. The full pass costs 1.7-3.8 ms at 50 KB and publications fit the cadence; correctness requires source dependency/state invalidation first.
Fix group-last CSS utilities: worthwhile direct Plate UI/Sync Shadcn performance work with the existing browser trigger. It does not call for a new public conversion or parsing API.

Reopen all HTML mapping design because remaining list/subtree loss exists: prefer a targeted accounting/content-fitting repair for the named cases. The surviving public laws and adopted encoder accounting do not need a universal codec.
proofLimits: Current public checks confirm projected TOC correctness for EditorStatic and renderStaticHtml without source mutation, and image-title preservation through serializeHtml/server parse. No full package suite, browser or new benchmark was run in this assessment. pp3 has 8 passing cells. The unmodified pp4 summarizer has 2 passes and 2 inconclusive attribution guards; the disclosed companion changes the sampled-CPU/trace-busy threshold from 1.20 to 1.25 and passes all 4. Retain observed timing/parity, but do not present the adjusted classification as an unchanged frozen gate. Root context gaps are supported by callback/static traversal source and the completed plan; the new root-context architecture remains to be designed and proven across live/static, content roots, root moves and state refresh. Current ledger check passed before this record. Historical streaming pending metadata alone is not evidence that parser adoption is undone.
